biography: Hervé Knapick, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in the rallycross paddocks, hails from the small village of Épernay, nestled in the heart of the Champagne region. Growing up, the roar of engines was as familiar as the popping of corks – his father, a local mechanic, maintained a fleet of rally cars for weekend enthusiasts. Hervé’s first taste of speed came at the age of 10, tearing through vineyard dirt tracks on a modified go-kart his father built. He quickly outgrew the kart, and at 16, he entered his first amateur rallycross event in a battered Peugeot 205, astonishing seasoned competitors with his raw talent and audacious driving style. A defining moment came at the 2018 French Rallycross Championship, where, against all odds, he wrestled his underpowered Citroen Saxo to victory, securing the attention of Citroen's junior team. Now, at 30, Knapick is at what many believe is his peak, a flamboyant force driving the Citroen DS3 RX, aiming for nothing less than world championship glory.
drivingStyle: Knapick's driving style is pure spectacle. He attacks corners with a ferocity that borders on recklessness, often flirting with the edge of control. He relies heavily on instinct and car control, favoring late braking and aggressive power application to sling his car through corners. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers squeezing every last ounce of performance out of his tires in a short, intense burst, often sacrificing longevity for immediate speed. Under pressure, Knapick either shines brilliantly or implodes spectacularly – there's rarely an in-between.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the 2021 World RX of Sweden, where Volkov accused Knapick of deliberate foul play.
A battle of the sexes and national pride. Dubois, a rising star from Belgium, has repeatedly challenged Knapick's dominance on the European circuit, leading to intense on-track battles.
A clash of styles. Tanaka's calculated, precise driving contrasts sharply with Knapick's flamboyant approach, creating a captivating rivalry whenever they share the track.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of vintage racing gloves given to him by his grandfather.
Listens to Édith Piaf's 'Non, je ne regrette rien' before every race.
Insists on personally polishing his Citroen DS3 RX's hood before each session, claiming it improves aerodynamics.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 World RX of France in front of his home crowd, a victory he dedicated to his late father, who had always dreamed of seeing him on the top step of the podium.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2020 World RX Championship finale while leading, handing the title to his rival, Viktor Volkov, in the process; a mistake that haunted him for months.
